correctness.rationale: The zero-truncated Poisson probability-generating function establishes the survivor and hazard. The gamma Mills-ratio integral has a sign-controlled derivative. The exact log-hazard derivative has positive prefactor times \(V(\lambda Q_\alpha)-(1+m_\alpha')\), with \(V\) strictly increasing. As \(t\downarrow0\), \(m_\alpha'\sim(1-\alpha)\Gamma(\alpha)t^{-\alpha}\) for \(0<\alpha<1\); as \(t\to\infty\), \(m_\alpha'\sim(1-\alpha)t^{-2}\) and \(Q_\alpha\sim t^{\alpha-1}e^{-t}/\Gamma(\alpha)\). The inverse-rate quotient diverges at both ends, hence its strictly positive minimum is attained. Analyticity handles equality and the intermediate sign reversal. Numerical checks independently corroborate the derivative identity but never substitute for the infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: The sharp phase boundary classifies decreasing-failure-rate versus interior-reversal regimes over the full three-parameter lifetime family motivated by hazard flexibility; proves the classification is invariant to rate/time scaling and gives a rigorous existence condition for both local min and max when the threshold is exceeded. A meaningful reliability-model selection criterion, not a simple reparameterization or isolated numerical instance.
